notes.title: Support for Fixed Cameras
notes.notes:
[i]Reality Mixer[/i] now supports [b]fixed[/b] cameras that are not attached to the headset.
You can use USB cameras or virtual cameras such as Camo, DroidCam, ManyCam, OBS-Camera, etc.

The video stream will be projected onto the side of a resizable box that you can place anywhere in the virtual world.
While playing a SteamVR game, the box will continue showing your video stream.

To use a fixed camera, first select and configure your camera, then uncheck the '[i]Attached to headset[/i]' checkbox and press the [i]Set Config[/i] button.
See the image below.

notes.title: Stereoscopic support for external USB cams, initial MJPG support
notes.notes:
Today's beta version (v.1.1.0.7) introduces support for stereoscopic streams when using external USB cameras. 
This version also has initial MJPG support.

To use a stereoscopic stream you need to edit the settings .xml file. (Please make a backup first.)
Replace the <cameras> part with the following lines:

[code]
<Cameras UseLeftCam="true" UseRightCam="true" UseLeftImageForBothEyes="false" UseRightImageForBothEyes="false">
	<Camera Name="3D USB Camera" UseAs="LeftCam" SensorWidth_Pixels="3840" SensorHeight_Pixels="1080" FramesPerSecond="30.0" Format="NV12" ImageLayout="Stereoscopic_SBS_LR"/>
	<Camera Name="3D USB Camera" UseAs="RightCam" SensorWidth_Pixels="3840" SensorHeight_Pixels="1080" FramesPerSecond="30.0" Format="NV12" ImageLayout="Stereoscopic_SBS_LR"/>
	<Camera Name="None" UseAs=""/>
</Cameras>
[/code]

Change the text "3D USB Camera" to the name of your camera.
Also change the resolution, [i]Format[/i] and [i]FramesPerSecond[/i] as needed.
To see what formats your camera supports, run the app once, then open the file "[i]VideoStreams.txt[/i]", which it creates next to the executable.

Remove the "[i]<Calibrations>[/i]" part, up to and including the "[i]</Calibrations>[/i]" tag.

More instructions are here:
https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1844610/view/4109043267624151513

notes.title: USB Camera Support (beta)
notes.notes:
[i]Reality Mixer[/i] now supports high-resolution USB cameras, displaying the camera image in VR.
[b]This is in beta[/b]. 
The feature has been tested with these two 4K cameras:
- Logitech BRIO
- Trust 4K Webcam

To activate the feature, you need to edit the settings file manually (for now).
The settings file, named similarly to 'RealityMixer_Settings_RoomId-0123456789ABCDEF.xml', resides in the same folder as the application's executable.
If you don't have a file with a RoomId (like '0123456789ABCDEF'), e.g. after a fresh install of the app, run [i]Reality Mixer[/i] at least once, while you're in VR. It will generate the settings file.

Edit the file in this way:
[list]
[*]Stop [i]SteamVR[/i].
[*]Make a backup of your settings file.
[*]Open the settings file in a text editor like [i]Notepad[/i].
[*]Find the tag that starts with "<[i]Cameras [/i]..."
[*]Remove all lines from that tag up to and including the line with "</[i]Cameras[/i]>".
[*]Replace these lines with:
[code]<Cameras UseLeftCam="true" UseRightCam="false" UseLeftImageForBothEyes="true">
	<Camera Name="Logitech BRIO" UseAs="LeftCam" SensorWidth_Pixels="3840" SensorHeight_Pixels="2160" FramesPerSecond="30.0" Format="NV12" ImageLayout="Monoscopic"/>
	<Camera Name="None" UseAs="RightCam"/>
</Cameras>[/code]
[*]Save the file, start [i]SteamVR[/i] and [i]Reality Mixer[/i].
[/list]
If you have a different camera, change the [i]Camera Name[/i] as shown above ("Logitech BRIO") to the name your camera uses, such as "Trust 4K Webcam". You can use a [i]Windows [/i]program such as [i]WebcamViewer [/i]to see the exact name of your camera.

You can change the resolution ([i]SensorWidth[/i] and [i]Height[/i]) and framerate ([i]FramesPerSecond[/i]) to values your camera supports.

Currently, the NV12 and YUY2 video formats are supported, so your camera must support one of those format (most do).

To improve the visual quality, increase the [i]TextureQuality[/i] parameter to 200 for each box. You'll find it in the "<[i]Box [/i]..." tags in the settings file.

This feature will be refined and enhanced.
If you experience any difficulties or have suggestions for improvement, please reach out!

notes.title: Discs instead of boxes
notes.notes:
With this update of [i]Reality Mixer[/i] you can have disc shaped portals.
[i]Discs[/i] work the same way as boxes. Click the button 'Disc' on [i]Reality Mixer[/i]'s page on the [i]SteamVR[/i] dashboard to create a disc that shows the camera passthrough.

This version also introduces the 'Look-at-me' feature. You can turn this on per box (and/or disc) on the [i]Box Edit Panel[/i] when editing the boxes/discs. When enabled, this feature keeps the front side of a box or disc pointed towards you.

notes.title: Reality Mixer now fully supports Windows Mixed Reality (WMR) headsets
notes.notes:
Reality Mixer now officially supports Windows Mixed Reality (WMR) headsets.

It's possible to use both cameras of the WMR headset, but you can also use just one. If you use both, it's best to align the left and right camera images so you get a correct stereoscopic view. This alignment is done on the [i]Camera Calibration[/i] screen. It uses one of your controllers to position the camera image. When performing the calibration, place the controller at the same distance from the headset as the object will be that you want to see in VR. E.g. when calibrating for a racing wheel, put the controller next the wheel and perform calibration while sitting in the same place you'll be when playing the game. This ensures correct stereo overlap at that distance.

Any questions? Just ask.

notes.title: Beta update: Camera Calibration tool
notes.notes:
Today's beta update (v. 0.14.0.6) features:
[list]
[*]A Camera Calibration screen where you can align the left and right camera images with real world objects. 
For calibration you need two controllers. One controller functions as the object that you will align the camera image with. For best results, place this controller at the same distance from the headset as the objects you want to see in VR. E.g., if you use the app to see a racing wheel, button box, HOTAS or airplane instrument panel, then place the controller next to those objects during calibration.
You need to be able to see the controller's 3D model in VR. Don't use the SteamVR Home with the mountain house, but use the older SteamVR Home (the empty space with stars and a mountain ridge in the distance).
There's an instruction page you can reach from the Camera Calibration page.
To get to the Camera Calibration page, follow the link on the Camera Setup page.
[/list]
If you're not on the Beta branch yet, go to your Steam library, right click the [i]Reality Mixer[/i] app, choose [i]Properties[/i], click the [i]BETAS[/i] tab and choose the beta branch from the drop down list.

notes.title: Profiles and auto-activation based on current game
notes.notes:
Reality Mixer has been updated with a much requested feature: Profiles and auto-activation.

You can create different profiles for different use cases such as:
[list]
[*] Seated games where you sit at your desktop.
[*] SimRacing where you have a mixed reality cockpit showing the real racing wheel and the insides of your real cockpit.
[*] Flightsims to see the real HOTAS.
[*] Couch experiences such as BigScreen so you can easily grab a drink or use a real keyboard using LapViewer.
[*] Room-scale games where you want to keep an eye on a real object in the room or use the FloorViewer.
[*] For streamers, setup a profile with a box around a streamdeck.
[/list]
A profile can contain up to eight Camera Boxes, Cockpits, Floor and/or Lap Viewers.
Profiles can be auto-activated when the app detects your run a specific game/app. E.g. configure it to activate the BigScreen profile when you start BigScreen, so you won't see the camera boxes around the HOTAS on your desk, because those are in another profile.

Tip: Setup an empty profile and make that the default auto-activation profile. Then games you have not added to a profile will not show any camera boxes. This can be useful if you only use Reality Mixer for the cockpit feature during Simracing, or only for DJing in VR Chat, etc.

notes.title: Update v.0.10.2.11
notes.notes:
Reality Mixer has been updated with the following changes:

[list]
[*]Activate a camera box using a button on your VR controller. Select a different, or the same, button for several camera boxes, the floor viewer, the lap viewer or cockpit. (This is in addition to the button activation using a keyboard or joystick button.)

Configure Voice Attack to press the same keyboard button as you have configured with "[b]Activate by button[/b]" in the Box Edit Panel.
[/list]

notes.title: Reality Mixer Update: New Activation Options, a Floor Viewer and a Lap Viewer
notes.notes:
This May 2022 update provides:
[list]
[*]Activate by [b][i]Gaze Angle[/i][/b]: Look straight at a camera box to make it visible. Use this activation method with seated games where you have things on a table next to your seat. The activation angle and optional activation delay can be configured. Using an activation delay means you have to look at the object for a second before it starts to show itself, to prevent accidental activation.
[*]Activate by [b][i]Button Press[/i][/b]: Press a keyboard, mouse, gamepad, HOTAS or racing wheel button to turn on/off a camera box.
[*][b][i]Floor Viewer[/i][/b]: To quickly see the real floor around your feet.
[*][b][i]Lap Viewer[/i][/b]: For use with seated experiences such as Big Screen. Lap Viewer can be used for quick glances at a normal (untracked) keyboard on your lap.
[*]Slider for camera brightness adjustment.
[*]Slider for camera contrast adjustment.
[*]Toggle for using transparency instead of static (white noise) for areas the camera can't see.
[/list]
[i]Floor Viewer[/i] and [i]Lap Viewer[/i] both use Gaze Angle Activation by default, but could use Proximity or ButtonPress activation as well.

If you have any questions, remarks or ideas, please share.

notes.title: Small update
notes.notes:
This is a small update consisting of:

[list]
[*]The UI panel for editing the camera boxes is now attached to a controller (or to the headset if only one controller is switched on). This removes the jumpiness of the panel.
[*]Fixed a bug where sometimes a camera image of another box side was shown.
[/list]
